title: Recombinant IL-38 Alleviates Temporomandibular Joint Synovial Inflammation via IL-1R1-NF-kappaB-IL1beta Pathway.
authors: Luo, Ping; Lv, Xueliang; Hui, Jifang; Qiao, Hu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究IL-38缓解颞下颌关节滑膜炎的炎症通路，核心为蛋白-蛋白互作与炎症机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION AND AIMS: Interleukin (IL)-38 has been identified as an anti-inflammatory cytokine; however, its specific role in temporomandibular joint (TMJ) synovial inflammation and the identity of its functional receptors remain elusive. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic efficacy of IL-38 in TMJ synovial inflammation and to elucidate its potential receptor mechanisms. METHODS: A rat model of temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJOA) was established via bilateral TMJ injection of mono-iodoacetate (MIA). Fifteen Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were randomly allocated into three groups: sham (PBS), model (MIA), and treatment (MIA +human recombinant IL-38, hIL-38). Protein BLAST analysis was utilized to predict IL-38 function and receptor affinity. Synovial histopathology was assessed using HE staining. Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) was employed to quantify inflammatory gene expression, while immunohistochemistry (IHC) was utilized to detect inflammatory proteins and IL-1 receptor type 1 (IL-1R1) expression. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network and protein-protein docking analyses were performed to predict the interaction between IL-38 and IL-1R1. RESULTS: IL-38 exhibited 43% identity and 55% positivity with interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra), its precursor, and its isoforms X1 and X2. HE staining demonstrated that hIL-38 significantly reduced synovial inflammatory cell infiltration. IHC staining revealed that hIL-38 inhibited macrophage infiltration (CD68(+)) and suppressed the expression of iNOS and COX-2, thereby attenuating synovial inflammation. Docking and PPI analyses corroborated a direct interaction between IL-38 and IL-1R1. Furthermore, IHC staining indicated that IL-38 down-regulated the protein levels of IL-1R1, NF-kappaB p65, and IL-1beta. CONCLUSIONS: IL-38 functions as a novel anti-inflammatory cytokine that alleviates TMJ synovial inflammation, potentially by antagonizing IL-1R1 and blocking the NF-kappaB signalling cascade. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: IL-38 may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for alleviating synovial inflammation in TMJOA.
abstract_zh: 引言与目的：白细胞介素（IL）-38已被鉴定为一种抗炎细胞因子；然而，其在颞下颌关节（TMJ）滑膜炎症中的具体作用及其功能性受体身份仍不明确。本研究旨在探讨IL-38在TMJ滑膜炎症中的治疗功效，并阐明其潜在受体机制。方法：通过双侧TMJ注射单碘乙酸（MIA）建立颞下颌关节骨关节炎（TMJOA）大鼠模型。将十五只Sprague-Dawley（SD）大鼠随机分为三组：假手术组（PBS）、模型组（MIA）和治疗组（MIA+人重组IL-38，hIL-38）。利用蛋白质BLAST分析预测IL-38功能和受体亲和力。采用HE染色评估滑膜组织病理学。使用定量实时PCR（qPCR）量化炎症基因表达，而免疫组织化学（IHC）用于检测炎症蛋白和IL-1受体1型（IL-1R1）表达。进行蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络和蛋白质-蛋白质对接分析，以预测IL-38与IL-1R1之间的相互作用。结果：IL-38与白细胞介素-1受体拮抗剂（IL-1Ra）及其前体和异构体X1和X2表现出43%的同一性和55%的阳性率。HE染色显示hIL-38显著减少滑膜炎症细胞浸润。IHC染色显示hIL-38抑制巨噬细胞浸润（CD68(+)）并抑制iNOS和COX-2的表达，从而减轻滑膜炎症。对接和PPI分析证实了IL-38与IL-1R1之间的直接相互作用。此外，IHC染色表明IL-38下调IL-1R1、NF-kappaB p65和IL-1beta的蛋白水平。结论：IL-38作为一种新型抗炎细胞因子，通过可能拮抗IL-1R1并阻断NF-kappaB信号级联反应来缓解TMJ滑膜炎症。临床相关性：IL-38可能为缓解TMJOA中的滑膜炎症提供一种新的治疗策略。
